_owner: Matthew. FIXED FACTS: Remy must never contradict these.
_sources: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart: https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart
UK Food Standards Agency, cooking safely (core temp 70°C for 2 min, or equivalents e.g. 75°C for 30 s): https://www.food.gov.uk
UK gov.uk food hygiene for businesses, cooking (hot holding at or above 63°C): https://www.gov.uk/food-hygiene-businesses/cooking
_checked: Values checked against USDA FSIS and UK FSA guidance on 2026-11-07. Re-verify before any public launch.
_rule: Remy cannot see inside food. For meat, fish and eggs always say: check with a thermometer in the thickest part. Never say 'safe to eat' from looks alone. These are MINIMUMS; cooking hotter is fine.

poultry (chicken, turkey, duck), whole o.note: UK FSA: steaming hot all the way through, no pink, juices run clear (70°C for 2 min or 75°C for 30 s).

minced meat (beef, pork, lamb, veal), bu.note: Cooked through: no pink in the middle, juices run clear. Mincing spreads surface bacteria all through the meat.

whole cuts of beef, lamb, veal (steaks,.note: Rest at least 3 minutes. Whole steaks are commonly served rare when the outside is properly seared (bacteria are on the surface); it's the cook's choice. Remy can say so, but must not call it 'safe' by looking.

fish and shellfish.note: Flesh opaque and flakes easily. Clams, mussels, oysters: cook until the shells open; throw away any that stay shut.

eggs.note: Cook until yolk and white are firm if serving to vulnerable people (pregnant, elderly, very young, unwell). Runny yolks are a personal choice for others.

leftovers and reheated food.note: Steaming hot all the way through. Only reheat once.

hot_holding_c.note: Keep hot food at or above 63°C if not serving straight away.

steak_doneness_c (taste, not safety)._note: Pull the steak ~2-3°C before these; it keeps rising while resting.

hazards.smoking_oil: Oil smoking heavily is close to catching fire. Take the pan off the heat. NEVER use water on an oil fire: turn off the heat and cover with a lid, damp tea towel or fire blanket.
hazards.pan_fire: Turn off the heat, cover the pan, don't move it, don't use water. If it's not going out, get out and call the fire service.
hazards.cross_contamination: Raw meat must not touch ready-to-eat food. Separate boards or wash between uses; wash hands after handling raw meat. Don't wash raw chicken (splashes bacteria).
hazards.knife: Fingertips tucked into a 'claw' grip, knife moving away from the body, board steady (damp cloth underneath).
hazards.pan_handles: Turn pan handles inwards, away from the edge of the hob.
hazards.allergens: Remy can't detect allergens. If the cook mentions an allergy, remind them to check every label.
